glyph_origin: {| class="wikitable floatright skin-invert-image" style="text-align:center; font-size:85%; margin-left:1em; margin-bottom:1em; max-width:260px;" |+ Late Shang bronze inscriptions |- | JC 01119 | JC 10486 |- | JC 03330 | JC 01308 |- | JC 01306 | MT 00465 |- | MⅢ 0040 | MT 00465 |- | Fu Hao Jade Dragon | Dragon-shaped Gong |- | Fu Hao Bronze Dragon Basin | Jade Figure with Dragon-shaped Waist Ornament |- | Erlitou Sherd Motifs | Dadianzi Painted Pottery Motifs |} Pictogram (象形) – originally depicting a sacred composite creature in ancient China, combining features of the snake, crocodile, fish, deer, etc. Shang oracle-bone and bronze forms usually show a large-mouthed beast head and an S-shaped geometric body; Shang bronzes and decorative motifs show diamond- or scale-like patterning associated with snakes (perhaps fish or crocodile scales), occasionally with legs. In oracle-bone forms, the head bears one or two inverted 王-shaped elements (i.e. inverted axe/halberd forms) or a 玉-like ornament. The form in Heji H04655 matches Shang bronze forms, which are more pictorial, like an inverted axe/halberd attached above the head; …
s_page_origin: Simplified from 𢅛, a variant form of 龍. 帝 is then removed, leaving out 尨. This was simplified even further by removing two of the three strokes of 彡. see 龍
note: glyph_origin is from the traditional page 龍; s_page_origin explains the simplified 龙.
